journal: Journal of Chemical Engineering of Japan 10(2), 89-94
title: Solubilities of sparingly soluble gases in aqueous sodium sulfate and sulfite solutions
experimental_method: Gas saturation (volumetric) method: degassed solution and measured gas volume in a dissolution vessel (Hg-sealed) in an air thermostat, gas buret and manometer; Ostwald coefficient L = VG/VL from gas absorbed and liquid volume, at gas partial pressure 1 atm.
uncertainties_stated: Pure-water results: average deviation 0.19-0.49 % over 7-18 determinations (Table 1). Mixed-salt data deviate <1 % from the interpolated values; Eq. (2) holds within 1 %.
quality_remarks: Ostwald coefficient per volume of liquid (salt solution), small liquid volume change from gas absorption corrected with partial molal volumes (O2 31, N2 40 cm3/mol). Vapour pressure of Na2SO3 solutions not available: Na2SO4 values (Timmermans) used at the same molarity, justified via Lantzke et al. isopiestic data. Sulfite solutions contained 96-98 mol % sulfite (rest sulfate); 'pure sulfite' solubility is therefore approximate. Authors note O2 in sulfite solution is not directly measurable because of oxidation (Table 7 is estimated). N2 pure-water value (0.01619) differs slightly from literature average (0.01589). Table 4 rows 0.778/0.785 mol/l: L 0.00808 and 0.00830 (text layer reads the second as 'O.OO83O'; image confirms 0.00830, non-monotonic as printed). Table 2 25 C has near-replicates 0.510/0.513 and 1.228/1.240.
